answer_1.quote: We begin by prompting the models to produce textual descriptions of a dish's appearance ...
answer_1.outputs: textual dish appearance descriptions, country‑of‑origin answers

answer_2.quote: We measure similarity between the generated and ground‑truth images collected in BORSch using the DiNOv2‑giant image encoder. We compute their cosine similarity. ... We calculate the Jaccard score per dish as each dish may have a varied number of countries as its origin.

answer_4.quote: To ensure the veracity of our evaluation pipeline, we perform human evaluation on a random sample of 400 model generated dish descriptions. A fluent annotator rates the quality of the pre‑translation descriptions from 0 to 1, scoring how well they visually describe the ground truth images.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate the quality of the description on a 0‑to‑1 scale based on how well it visually matches the ground‑truth image.
